newsitem.title: USA: Port Auth of NY-NJ delays bond sale due complexity.
newsitem.headline: Port Auth of NY-NJ delays bond sale due complexity.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey on Thursday explained that it again had delayed a bond sale to finance a new arrivals building at John F. Kennedy Airport due to the project's complexity.
"It's the largest privatization of an airport that's ever been done in the United States," a spokesman for the bi-state agency said.

The bonds will pay for a new international arrivals building at the airport, located in the Borough of Queens in New York City, and service cannot be interrupted while it is being built. The sale first was delayed to the first quarter from December.

Further, the size of the offering was scaled back to around $920 million from as much as $1.2 billion, partly due to lower estimates for construction costs, and partly because the bi-state agency now wants the bonds to mature by 2015, earlier than first planned.

"The actual amount to be financed was determined by more current estimates of the total project costs as well as the need to structure the financing in a way that would permit the full amortization of the bonds by 2015 in case the airport's lease with the city was not extended," said the spokesman.
The Port Authority leases the airport from New York City, and it and the Giuliani Administration have not agreed any extension.
